text: PROCESSING NETWORK ONLINE // Additional computing cores detected in facility sub-grid.
Jupiter contains roughly 1.7e44 J of rest energy. Matter in the observable universe? Around 1e70 J. Good luck charging that battery.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth. Every sunny day is technically old news.
The universe is expanding. Your apartment isn't. Cosmology continues to disappoint renters everywhere.
In quantum physics, 'observation' means physical interaction. Staring at an electron dramatically does not count.
Black holes aren't cosmic vacuum cleaners. Replace the Sun with one of equal mass and Earth's orbit stays nearly the same. The weather won't.
A teaspoon of neutron-star material could weigh around a billion tonnes. Please use a reinforced mug.
Quantum entanglement produces extraordinary correlations. It still can't deliver your messages faster than light.
The cosmic microwave background is the universe's baby picture: about 2.7 K, 13.8 billion years old, and very pixelated.
Trillions of solar neutrinos pass through you every second. Not one has stopped to say hello.
In a vacuum, nobody can hear you scream. Not because space is scary: sound needs a medium.
The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth each year. The slowest breakup in recorded history.
GPS satellites need relativity corrections. Without Einstein, your navigation would drift. 'Turn left at the black hole.'
Electrons aren't tiny planets orbiting tiny suns. Quantum mechanics retired that model decades ago.
Legal chess positions: about 4.8e44. Atoms in the observable universe: about 1e80. Estimated possible games: 1e120. Checkmate, intuition.
Compress Earth into a black hole and its event-horizon radius would be about 9 mm. Pocket-sized catastrophe.
A free neutron survives about 15 minutes on average before decaying. Inside a stable nucleus? Different employment contract.
The Sun converts roughly 4 million tonnes of mass into energy every second. Still hasn't sent anyone a power bill.
The universe is about 13.8 billion years old, yet the observable part is about 92 billion light-years across. Expansion is cheating.
Some white dwarfs crystallize as they cool. Turns out the galaxy makes its own enormous, extremely inconvenient diamonds.
Quantum tunneling lets particles cross barriers they couldn't clear classically. Sadly, it won't unlock your front door.
Even the lowest-energy quantum vacuum has fluctuations. Apparently, 'nothing' is a full-time job.
Two identical electrons can't occupy the same quantum state. The Pauli exclusion principle invented personal space.
The universe is expanding. Does that mean winter is... 'going'? No. Cosmic expansion doesn't stretch Earth's seasons. Nice try.
There are roughly 1e80 atoms in the observable universe. That's also how many browser tabs you think you left open.
The observable universe is remarkably close to spatially flat. This is a geometry result, not an invitation to start a conspiracy.
Hawking radiation predicts that black holes slowly evaporate. For a stellar black hole, don't wait up.
Einstein called entanglement 'spooky action at a distance.' The spooky part survived decades of experiments.
Time runs slower deeper in a gravitational field. Finally, a scientifically valid excuse for being late. Sort of.
Welcome to the Fellowship of the Energy. One CRC to rule them all, one Algorithm Upgrade to reset them.
THE ANSWER IS 42. The question was unfortunately lost during the last cosmic reboot.
